name: Collision-shape forgiveness
summary: Gameplay collision can use stable, intention-oriented shapes instead of matching every visual pixel or animation pose.
player_action: The player moves near corners, narrow openings, ledges, ceilings, and walls while attempting another movement action.
system_response: Simplified collision and bounded correction prevent low-information edge contacts from canceling an otherwise valid action.

weakened_by: visual silhouettes that imply a different boundary

failure_modes: Invisible gaps between visual art and collision make contact appear false.
Aggressive correction pushes the player into hazards or through intended blockers.
Per-object exceptions become impossible to reason about.
Animation-driven hitboxes change locomotion boundaries unpredictably.
accessibility: Use redundant edge and hazard silhouettes.
Test at reduced visual acuity and under camera motion.
Offer debug captures that show correction events.

smallest_playable_test.setup: Place one strict rectangular controller and one corrected controller in the same corner, doorway, stair, and low-ceiling course.
smallest_playable_test.retain_if: Snags fall while visible disagreement and false pass-through remain rare and explainable.
smallest_playable_test.revise_if: Traversal improves only on some orientations or frame rates.
smallest_playable_test.reject_if: Correction creates new hazards, skips, or boundaries that players cannot see.

evidence.claim: Celeste uses corner correction to avoid rejecting near-valid jumps at obstacle corners.
evidence.notes: This supports bounded correction, not arbitrary collision removal.
